app.name: Warren
header.corte_help: Nothing on this page was published after this date.
inicio.title: Warren
inicio.lede: Warren's screens will live here, one per question. They are coming soon.
bench.title: Test components
bench.lede: This page is for checking how the side panel works with a keyboard, a screen reader and on a phone. It shows no figures.
panel.label: Figure details
panel.tab_error: We could not load this section. Try again in a few seconds.
panel.body.fuente: Where the figure comes from will go here: for a reported figure, the filing, tag, period and filing date; for an estimate, the run, its cut-off date and the source of each assumption.
panel.body.formula: The calculation's steps will go here, with the formula you would type in your spreadsheet.
panel.body.concepto: What the figure means will go here, for example what net debt is.
panel.body.ysi: Here you will be able to change a model assumption and see what moves. A reported figure cannot be edited.
panel.body.leer: Headlines published before the cut-off date, and related companies, will go here.
error.corte.title: The cut-off date is not valid
error.corte.body: The link has a date that cannot be read. Use year-month-day, for example 2026-11-03.
error.busy.title: Warren is saving data
error.busy.body: The database is busy with a long download. Wait a few seconds and try again.
error.not_found.title: We could not find that section
error.not_found.body: The link asks for a figure or a tab this page does not have.
card.ask.reader_unsure: I'm not sure I understood your question. Check the reading or choose from the menus.
card.ask.company_missing: Which company do you mean? Warren covers eight: {companies}.
card.ask.value_range: You wrote a range ({text}) for {input}. Which value do you want to try, or would you rather see the sensitivity table?
card.ask.value_missing: Which value do you want to try for {input}? You can also see the sensitivity table.
card.ask.value_missing_via: How big is the Fed's move? Write it in basis points.
card.ask.value_ambiguous: Is “{text}” {first} or {second}? Some countries use the point for thousands and others for decimals.
card.ask.value_unreadable: I couldn't read the value “{text}” for {input}. Write it as a number.
card.ask.driver_periods: Do you change {input} for next year only, or for every forecast year?
card.ask.method_unknown: Warren computes the terminal value with its own method or with Gordon's; it has no exit-multiple method. Which one do you want?
card.note.corte_default: Cutoff date: {date}, the last day that has ended in New York. Nothing you will see was published after it.
card.note.corte_from_question: Cutoff date: {date}, the one I read in your question. Please confirm it.
card.note.fed_move_is_event: The value is the Fed's move, not the risk-free rate's. Warren turns it into a change in the 10-year Treasury yield with a range from published studies, never one for one.
card.note.cash_unchanged: You change only the shares outstanding: the cash that would be paid or received stays the same. So value per share moves without anyone paying or receiving anything, which does not happen in real life. For a buyback, change debt: Warren adjusts the shares with it.
card.note.wacc_bypasses_parts: With WACC set directly, Warren stops using its components: beta, the risk-free rate, the equity risk premium, the cost of debt, the tax shield and the weights of debt and equity.
card.note.usd_only: Warren reports in US dollars, as these companies file their financial statements. It doesn't convert currencies.
card.note.intrinsic_value_offer: Warren doesn't forecast prices or say whether to buy. I'll show you its intrinsic value, its range and which assumptions it depends on.
card.note.intrinsic_value_offer_target: Warren doesn't compute a target price or say whether to buy. I'll show you its intrinsic value, its range and which assumptions it depends on.
input.debt_tax_rate: the tax rate on the debt tax shield
card.ask.value_currency: You wrote “{text}” in another currency. Warren doesn't convert currencies: write the amount in US dollars.
card.ask.percent_or_points: You wrote “{text}” for {input}. Is that percentage points (say, from 20% to 10%) or a share of its level (from 20% to 18%)?
card.ask.points_or_bp: You wrote “{text}” for {input}. Is that percentage points or basis points (100 bp = 1 point)?
card.ask.fed_surprise: Does the Fed's move surprise the market, or was it expected? What was expected is already in the bond yield on the cutoff date and barely moves it; only the unexpected part does.
card.ask.wacc_and_parts: You set WACC and also change one of its components. With WACC fixed, that change would have no effect. Which do you want to use?
card.note.relative_change: I read “{text}” as a relative change in {input}: a share of its current level, not percentage points.
